title: The Art of the Oxford
excerpt: Inside the hand-stitching and finishing that separates a real oxford from an imitation.
content: A great oxford starts with a single hide of full-grain leather, cut by hand around a wooden last. What follows — the closed lacing, the hand-finished edge, the leather sole built to be resoled rather than replaced — is the difference between a shoe you wear for a season and one you wear for a decade.

author: ALEXANDRIS Journal

title: Caring for Leather, Season After Season
excerpt: A simple routine that keeps full-grain leather looking new for years.
content: Wipe every pair clean after wear, condition the leather every few months, and always let a wet shoe dry away from direct heat. A little care, repeated often, does more for a shoe's lifespan than any single treatment.
author: ALEXANDRIS Journal

title: How to Style Ankle Boots, Three Ways
excerpt: From tailored trousers to a slip dress, the ankle boot's quiet versatility.
content: A black leather ankle boot is one of the few pairs that moves convincingly between a desk, a dinner, and a weekend away. Cropped trousers keep the silhouette clean; a slip dress plays the boot's structure against something softer.
author: ALEXANDRIS Journal

title: Inside the Atelier
excerpt: A look at the small workshop where every ALEXANDRIS pair begins.
content: Every pair passes through the same small team, from the first cut of leather to the final polish. It is slower than a factory line, and that is the point.
author: ALEXANDRIS Journal
